picks.editorial_note: An international team led by TU Wien physicist Mario Krenn showed in Nature that AI can design novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups — a striking demonstration of AI accelerating fundamental scientific discovery itself, not just analyzing data.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen and international collaborators published HydroGym in Nature, a reinforcement-learning platform for actively controlling fluid dynamics with direct applications spanning energy, transportation, and defense systems.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's Generalist-Specialist Collaboration framework pairs a broad medical AI model with lightweight specialist models, offering a scalable path toward more precise, deployable clinical AI systems.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: EPFL researchers trained AI systems to express calibrated 'doubt' when proposing experiments, a meaningful step toward AI that knows the limits of its own confidence — critical for trustworthy scientific automation.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: NSF is funding a new $30 million Science and Technology Center, led by Michigan State with Georgia Tech among eight partner institutions, to advance predictive turbulence modeling for energy and flight applications — a major multi-institutional science investment.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: A $7.7 million federal partnership between Kansas engineers, the Army Corps of Engineers, and DHS is building AI-integrated digital twins to inspect and protect American dams — critical infrastructure security work with direct public-safety stakes.
picks.title: Four years later KU researchers continue their work strengthening American dams

picks.editorial_note: A $2.88 million DOE award to a University of Houston-led coalition targets AI-driven discovery of next-generation magnets to reduce U.S. reliance on foreign-controlled critical mineral supply chains — a direct link between AI research and national economic security policy.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin is launching interdisciplinary fusion energy seed grants tied to the DOE's Genesis Mission, reflecting a broader federal push to apply AI toward accelerating fusion energy development.
picks.title: Fusion Energy Seed Grants Launch New Interdisciplinary Collaborations at UT Austin - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen secured a nationwide German permit to test its Level 4 autonomous research vehicle on public roads — a significant regulatory milestone for real-world autonomous driving research in Europe.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: UNSW Canberra opened one of Australia's largest indoor robotics and drone testing arenas, creating shared infrastructure that links academic researchers with industry and government defense partners.
picks.title: New facilities expand innovation ecosystem at UNSW Canberra City
